newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Analysts' views on MoDo 9-mth results.
newsitem.headline: Analysts' views on MoDo 9-mth results.

text.p: Following are comments from analysts on Sweden's forestry industry after MoDo posted a 43 percent slump in nine month profits at 2.47 billion crowns after financial items.
(MoDo) was better than expected and most of the improvement came from the operational side. Iggesund's new cartonboard machine has reached production earlier than expected.
Currency positions were good but MoDo has been very open about them and the market was expecting this.
I expect NorScan inventory stocks for October to be up at between 1.80 and 1.90 million tonnes.
The most surprising element (of MoDo's nine-month result) was printing paper. The division's result improved at the same time as prices fell.
HAKAN OSTLING, OF GOLDMAN SACHS IN LONDON.
AssiDoman's nine-month report reflected the uncertain overall outlook for the economy and pulp and paper industry.

The market may have taken some comfort that the result did meet expectations and that all business areas are making money again. In addition, all pulp and paper stocks were strong yesterday as a reaction to very weak performance in the recent past.

Pulp prices could fall by between $50 and $100 a tonne in the next few months. This is partly because of lower prices in the Far East, where net buyer China is selling into the market. Also, operation rates especially in North America have been too high, and pulp mills in the Nordic countries cannot close down in winter because they would freeze up.
I predict NorScan inventories at end-October at more than 1.80 million tonnes.
There is a short-term risk of pulp prices going down.
